# Model and source

```{r model-load}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Felton_2014_piperacillin"))
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.02664-14>

Felton 2014 fitted four two-compartment structural models to pooled
piperacillin data from 146 critically ill adults with the nonparametric
adaptive grid (NPAG) algorithm of Pmetrics 1.1.1 (Fig. 2, equations 1a-1d):
linear clearance, Michaelis-Menten clearance, parallel linear and
Michaelis-Menten clearance, and linear clearance with creatinine clearance on
clearance and body weight on central volume. The Michaelis-Menten model had the
best likelihood (Table 2), but all four fitted well and the authors carried the
**linear model with covariates** into the BestDose dose-optimisation software
as "the most clinically relevant model". That model is the only one whose
parameter estimates are published (Table 3), and it is the one packaged here.
The other three appear in Table 2 only as fit statistics, with no parameter
values, so they cannot be reconstructed.

**Solve this model with `useLinCmt = FALSE`.** Its `model()` block exposes the
micro-constants `k12` and `k21` and no `q` / `vp` pair, so the default
ODE-to-`linCmt()` conversion has no two-compartment macro-parameterisation to
build and would drop `peripheral1`.

# Population

The estimation data set pooled three previously published studies (Felton 2014
Materials and Methods and Table 1): 94 surgical patients from Lodise et al.
(76 given 2 g over 30 min with sampling in the first dosing interval, and 18
colorectal-surgery patients given 4 g over 30 min every 6 h with sampling in the
first two intervals), 12 hospitalised patients from Felton et al. given 3 g over
4 h every 8 h and sampled mainly on day 3, and 40 ventilated patients with
ventilator-associated pneumonia from Boselli et al. given 12 or 16 g/day by
continuous infusion and sampled during the second 24 h. In total 803 plasma
concentrations (2 to 10 per patient) were available.

Across the combined cohort (Table 1), mean age was 55.8 years (range 18 to 88),
mean weight 71.7 kg (median 69.0, range 38.1 to 122.5), mean Cockcroft-Gault
creatinine clearance 85.9 mL/min (median 81.0, range 14.0 to 245.7), and 59 of
146 patients (40.4%) were female.

The external validation cohort of Roberts et al. (8 critically ill patients,
4 g over 20 min every 6 or 8 h) had markedly higher renal function (mean
creatinine clearance 165.5 mL/min, range 58.8 to 256.6) and weight (mean 86.8
kg, range 72 to 132); it was not used for estimation.

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Felton_2014_piperacillin.R`
carries an in-file comment pointing at its source location; they are collected
here.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(central)` | n/a | Fig. 2, equation 1d: `dX1/dt = R(1) - ((Cli + Cr_cl * Cls) / (Vi + Wt * Vs) + kcp) * X1 + kpc * X2` |
| `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Fig. 2, equation 2: `dX2/dt = kcp * X1 - kpc * X2` |
| `cl` | n/a | Fig. 2, equation 1d numerator: `Cli + Cr_cl * Cls` |
| `vc` | n/a | Fig. 2, equation 1d denominator: `Vi + Wt * Vs` |
| `Cc` | n/a | Fig. 2 legend: X1 in mg, Vc in L, concentrations in mg/L |
| `lcl_nonren` | `log(3.83)` | Table 3, `Cli` mean 3.83 [median 2.79] +/- 3.35 |
| `e_crcl_cl_renal` | `0.11` | Table 3, `Cls` mean 0.11 [0.10] +/- 0.07 |
| `lvc` | `log(4.54)` | Table 3, `Vi` mean 4.54 [1.83] +/- 4.43 |
| `e_wt_vc` | `0.12` | Table 3, `Vs` mean 0.12 [0.06] +/- 0.12 |
| `lk12` | `log(6.74)` | Table 3, `kcp` mean 6.74 [0.85] +/- 11.38 |
| `lk21` | `log(9.14)` | Table 3, `kpc` mean 9.14 [1.65] +/- 13.13 |
| `etalcl_nonren` | `0.568181` | Table 3, `Cli`: `log(1 + (3.35/3.83)^2)` |
| `etae_crcl_cl_renal` | `0.340008` | Table 3, `Cls`: `log(1 + (0.07/0.11)^2)` |
| `etalvc` | `0.668921` | Table 3, `Vi`: `log(1 + (4.43/4.54)^2)` |
| `etae_wt_vc` | `0.693147` | Table 3, `Vs`: `log(1 + (0.12/0.12)^2)` |
| `etalk12` | `1.348277` | Table 3, `kcp`: `log(1 + (11.38/6.74)^2)` |
| `etalk21` | `1.119609` | Table 3, `kpc`: `log(1 + (13.13/9.14)^2)` |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | `1.04`, `0.14` | Materials and Methods, "Development of a population pharmacokinetic model": assay error polynomial `SD = 1.04 + (0.14 x C)` |
| `CRCL` | covariate | Table 1, estimated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault, mL/min) |
| `WT` | covariate | Table 1, weight (kg) |

The printed constants are restated once here and every check below uses them,
so that the checks are driven by numbers transcribed from the paper rather than
by the model's own variables.

```{r paper-constants}
paper_mean <- list(cli = 3.83, cls = 0.11, vi = 4.54, vs = 0.12, kcp = 6.74, kpc = 9.14) # Table 3 means
paper_median <- list(cli = 2.79, cls = 0.10, vi = 1.83, vs = 0.06, kcp = 0.85, kpc = 1.65) # Table 3 medians

paper_cl <- function(crcl, p = paper_mean) p$cli + p$cls * crcl
paper_vc <- function(wt, p = paper_mean) p$vi + p$vs * wt

ui_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
```

# Deterministic structural checks

## Clearance and central volume versus the covariates

Clearance and central volume are additive linear functions of creatinine
clearance and body weight (Fig. 2, equation 1d). The intercepts are the values
extrapolated to zero creatinine clearance or zero weight, not typical-patient
values, and nothing is centred on a reference value.

```{r check-covariates}
grid <- tidyr::crossing(CRCL = c(14, 50, 81, 120, 165.5, 245.7), WT = c(38.1, 69, 122.5)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev_grid <- grid |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 1)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central")

chk_cov <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui_typ, events = as.data.frame(ev_grid), keep = c("CRCL", "WT"), useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"),
  # A multi-subject solve of the zeroRe() model warns that it has no omega;
  # that is intended for a typical-value grid.
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
) |>
  distinct(id, CRCL, WT, cl, vc) |>
  mutate(cl_paper = paper_cl(CRCL), vc_paper = paper_vc(WT))

# Deterministic algebra: the model must reproduce equation 1d exactly.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(chk_cov$cl - chk_cov$cl_paper) / chk_cov$cl_paper) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(chk_cov$vc - chk_cov$vc_paper) / chk_cov$vc_paper) < 1e-8
)

chk_cov |>
  filter(WT == 69) |>
  select(CRCL, cl_paper, cl) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Creatinine clearance (mL/min)" = CRCL,
    "CL, equation 1d (L/h)" = cl_paper,
    "CL, model (L/h)" = cl
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical clearance across the observed creatinine-clearance range.")
```

```{r figure-covariates}
tibble(CRCL = seq(14, 245.7, length.out = 100)) |>
  mutate(CL = paper_cl(CRCL)) |>
  ggplot(aes(CRCL, CL)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance (mL/min)", y = "Typical clearance (L/h)",
    title = "Clearance versus creatinine clearance",
    caption = "Fig. 2 equation 1d with the Table 3 means over the observed range (Table 1)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Whole-ODE check against an independent biexponential

The two-compartment infusion system has a closed-form solution. The function
below is written from the paper's printed constants and is independent of the
packaged model, so agreement exercises the ODEs, the infusion route and the
observation equation together. It also detects a dropped peripheral
compartment, which leaves `Dose / CL` intact while changing the curve.

```{r closed-form}
biexp_conc <- function(times, crcl, wt, dose, tinf, p = paper_mean) {
  cl <- paper_cl(crcl, p)
  vc <- paper_vc(wt, p)
  k10 <- cl / vc
  b <- k10 + p$kcp + p$kpc
  alpha <- (b + sqrt(b^2 - 4 * k10 * p$kpc)) / 2
  beta <- (b - sqrt(b^2 - 4 * k10 * p$kpc)) / 2
  rate <- dose / tinf
  ca <- (alpha - p$kpc) / ((alpha - beta) * alpha)
  cb <- (p$kpc - beta) / ((alpha - beta) * beta)
  # Central amount under a never-ending infusion started u ago; a finite
  # infusion is that minus the same thing started tinf later.
  step <- function(u) ifelse(u <= 0, 0, rate * (ca * (1 - exp(-alpha * pmax(u, 0))) + cb * (1 - exp(-beta * pmax(u, 0)))))
  list(conc = (step(times) - step(times - tinf)) / vc, alpha = alpha, beta = beta, cl = cl)
}

t_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)
ref <- biexp_conc(t_grid, crcl = 81, wt = 69, dose = 4000, tinf = 0.5)

ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 4000, rate = 4000 / 0.5, cmt = "central"),
  tibble(id = 1L, time = t_grid, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
) |>
  mutate(CRCL = 81, WT = 69)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_typ, events = as.data.frame(ev_typ), useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot("peripheral1" %in% names(sim_typ))

cmp_typ <- tibble(time = t_grid, model = sim_typ$Cc, closed = ref$conc) |> filter(time > 0, time <= 12)
rel_err <- max(abs(cmp_typ$model - cmp_typ$closed) / cmp_typ$closed)

# Deterministic: two solutions of the same linear ODE.
stopifnot(rel_err < 1e-4)

# Mass balance: AUC from 0 to infinity equals Dose / CL.
auc_model <- sum(diff(sim_typ$time) * (head(sim_typ$Cc, -1) + tail(sim_typ$Cc, -1)) / 2) +
  tail(sim_typ$Cc, 1) / ref$beta
stopifnot(abs(auc_model / (4000 / ref$cl) - 1) < 0.01)

tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Typical CL at 81 mL/min (L/h)", "Typical Vc at 69 kg (L)",
    "alpha half-life (h)", "beta half-life (h)", "Dose / CL (mg*h/L)", "Model AUC0-inf (mg*h/L)"
  ),
  Value = c(ref$cl, paper_vc(69), log(2) / ref$alpha, log(2) / ref$beta, 4000 / ref$cl, auc_model)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical patient (median creatinine clearance 81 mL/min, median weight 69 kg), 4 g over 30 min.")
```

# Mean or median as the typical value

Table 3 reports, for each parameter, the mean, median and SD of its NPAG
marginal distribution, and the means and medians differ several-fold for the
volume and distribution terms (`kcp` 6.74 vs 0.85 1/h; `Vi` 4.54 vs 1.83 L).
The paper does not say which column describes a typical patient. The only
population-level data it shows are the observed first-dose concentrations of
the 8 external validation patients in Fig. 4 (filled circles; 4 g over 20 min).
Those points were digitised by the maintainers by eye from the published
figure and are accurate to roughly 5-10 mg/L; they are used here only to
choose between two columns that differ several-fold.

```{r fig4-data}
fig4 <- tribble(
  ~patient, ~time, ~conc,
  1, 0.5, 170, 1, 1, 110, 1, 2, 80, 1, 3, 62, 1, 4.5, 40, 1, 6.5, 15,
  2, 0.5, 120, 2, 1.2, 40, 2, 2, 15, 2, 3, 8, 2, 5, 3, 2, 6, 2,
  3, 0.5, 55, 3, 1, 18, 3, 1.5, 12, 3, 2, 8, 3, 2.5, 6, 3, 4.5, 3,
  4, 0.5, 165, 4, 1, 75, 4, 1.5, 40, 4, 2, 30, 4, 4, 5, 4, 6, 2,
  5, 0.5, 115, 5, 1, 45, 5, 2, 25, 5, 3, 20, 5, 4, 12, 5, 6, 7,
  6, 0.5, 88, 6, 1, 43, 6, 1.5, 32, 6, 2, 25, 6, 2.5, 15, 6, 4, 8,
  7, 0.5, 180, 7, 1, 100, 7, 1.5, 70, 7, 2, 50, 7, 4, 25, 7, 6, 12,
  8, 0.5, 195, 8, 1, 85, 8, 2, 70, 8, 3, 50, 8, 4, 28, 8, 5.5, 15
)
roberts <- list(crcl = 165.5, wt = 86.8, dose = 4000, tinf = 20 / 60) # Table 1 and Methods
```

The typical-value profile at the validation cohort's mean covariates is
computed once with the means (the packaged model) and once with the medians.

```{r mean-vs-median}
t_fine <- sort(unique(c(fig4$time, seq(0, 8, by = 0.05))))
ev_rob <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = roberts$dose, rate = roberts$dose / roberts$tinf, cmt = "central"),
  tibble(id = 1L, time = t_fine, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
) |>
  mutate(CRCL = roberts$crcl, WT = roberts$wt)

ui_median <- rxode2::ini(
  ui_typ,
  lcl_nonren = log(paper_median$cli), e_crcl_cl_renal = paper_median$cls,
  lvc = log(paper_median$vi), e_wt_vc = paper_median$vs,
  lk12 = log(paper_median$kcp), lk21 = log(paper_median$kpc)
)

prof <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui_typ, events = as.data.frame(ev_rob), useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(column = "Table 3 means (packaged)"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui_median, events = as.data.frame(ev_rob), useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(column = "Table 3 medians")
) |>
  select(column, time, Cc)

fit <- fig4 |>
  mutate(
    pred_mean = approx(prof$time[prof$column == "Table 3 means (packaged)"], prof$Cc[prof$column == "Table 3 means (packaged)"], time)$y,
    pred_median = approx(prof$time[prof$column == "Table 3 medians"], prof$Cc[prof$column == "Table 3 medians"], time)$y
  )

late <- fit |> filter(time >= 2)
lr_mean <- median(log(late$conc / late$pred_mean))
lr_median <- median(log(late$conc / late$pred_median))

# Deterministic (typical values against fixed digitised points). The means
# miss the observed median by under 2-fold from 2 h on; the medians miss it by
# more than 3-fold, because their small Vi, Vs and kcp give a half-life near
# 0.7 h.
stopifnot(
  abs(lr_mean) < log(2),
  lr_median > log(3),
  abs(lr_mean) < abs(lr_median)
)

tibble(
  Column = c("Table 3 means (packaged)", "Table 3 medians"),
  "Median observed / predicted, t >= 2 h" = exp(c(lr_mean, lr_median))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Digitised Fig. 4 first-dose concentrations versus the typical-value profile at the validation cohort's mean covariates.")
```

```{r figure-mean-vs-median}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = filter(prof, time > 0), aes(time, Cc, colour = column), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig4, aes(time, conc), shape = 16, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of first dose (h)", y = "Piperacillin (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical-value profile, 4 g over 20 min",
    caption = "Points: first-dose observations of the 8 validation patients, digitised from Fig. 4 of Felton 2014.\nLines: typical patient at creatinine clearance 165.5 mL/min and weight 86.8 kg."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The means were therefore taken as typical values. Even with them, the typical
profile sits below most observations after 2 h; the validation patients'
individual covariates are not published, so this is compared at the cohort
means only, and the stochastic check below is the fairer test.

# Virtual cohorts

## Validation cohort (Fig. 4)

A cohort of 200 virtual patients with covariates resembling the Roberts
validation cohort receives one 4 g dose over 20 min. The 5th, 50th and 95th
percentiles of the simulated individual concentrations are compared with the
digitised Fig. 4 points.

```{r vpc-validation}
# set.seed() seeds R's RNG, which draws the covariates below. rxSetSeed()
# seeds rxode2's eta sampler, whose draws can still differ across rxode2 builds
# and thread counts, so the assertion is on a coverage fraction with headroom.
set.seed(20140505)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20140505)
n_sub <- 200L

subj_rob <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  CRCL = pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(n_sub, 165.5, 50), 58.8), 256.6), # Table 1 Roberts: mean 165.5, range 58.8-256.6
  WT = pmin(pmax(stats::rlnorm(n_sub, log(82.5), 0.15), 72), 132) # Table 1 Roberts: median 82.5, range 72-132
)
ev_vpc <- subj_rob |>
  tidyr::crossing(bind_rows(
    tibble(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = roberts$dose, rate = roberts$dose / roberts$tinf),
    tibble(time = seq(0.25, 8, by = 0.25), evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
  )) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_rob <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui, events = as.data.frame(ev_vpc), useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame")

pi_rob <- sim_rob |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

cover <- fig4 |>
  mutate(tt = round(time * 4) / 4) |>
  left_join(pi_rob, by = c(tt = "time")) |>
  mutate(inside = conc >= lo & conc <= hi)

# Robust envelope check: about 90% of the digitised points fall inside the
# simulated 90% interval; 75% leaves room for cohort-to-cohort variation.
stopifnot(mean(cover$inside) > 0.75)
mean(cover$inside)
```

```{r figure-vpc-validation}
ggplot(pi_rob, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = med), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(data = fig4, aes(time, conc), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5, 400)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of first dose (h)", y = "Piperacillin (mg/L)",
    title = "First dose in the validation cohort",
    caption = "Band: simulated 5th-95th percentiles (200 virtual patients); line: median.\nPoints: digitised first-dose observations from Fig. 4 of Felton 2014."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Development-cohort regimens

The four regimens of the estimation data set are simulated in a cohort whose
creatinine clearance and weight follow the Table 1 combined column
(log-normal around the medians, with spreads chosen so the means match, and
truncated to the observed ranges).

```{r cohort-dev}
set.seed(20140701)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20140701)

# Log-normal spread s chosen so that median * exp(s^2 / 2) equals the Table 1 mean.
s_crcl <- sqrt(2 * log(85.9 / 81.0))
s_wt <- sqrt(2 * log(71.7 / 69.0))

regimens <- tribble(
  ~treatment, ~amt, ~tinf, ~tau, ~ndose,
  "2 g over 30 min, single dose", 2000, 0.5, 24, 1,
  "4 g over 30 min q6h", 4000, 0.5, 6, 8,
  "3 g over 4 h q8h", 3000, 4, 8, 6,
  "16 g/day continuous infusion", 16000, 24, 24, 2
)

ev_dev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  subj <- tibble(
    id = (i - 1L) * n_sub + seq_len(n_sub),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(stats::rlnorm(n_sub, log(81.0), s_crcl), 14.0), 245.7),
    WT = pmin(pmax(stats::rlnorm(n_sub, log(69.0), s_wt), 38.1), 122.5),
    treatment = r$treatment
  )
  dose <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = r$tau * seq(0, r$ndose - 1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = r$amt, rate = r$amt / r$tinf)
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 48, by = 0.25)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
  bind_rows(dose, obs)
})) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_dev <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui,
  events = as.data.frame(ev_dev), keep = c("treatment", "CRCL"),
  useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r figure-dev}
sim_dev |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Piperacillin (mg/L)",
    title = "Simulated regimens of the estimation data set",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of 200 virtual patients per regimen."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Continuous-infusion steady state

At steady state a continuous infusion gives `Css = R0 / CL` exactly. The
typical-value model is checked against that closed form, and the simulated
cohort's median concentration at 48 h is checked against the cohort's own
median `R0 / CL`, since clearance is linear and the per-subject ratio is exact
once distribution has equilibrated.

```{r check-css}
r0 <- 16000 / 24
ev_ci <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = 1L, time = c(0, 24), evid = 1L, amt = 16000, rate = 16000 / 24),
  tibble(id = 1L, time = c(24, 48), evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", CRCL = 81, WT = 69) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))
css_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_typ, events = as.data.frame(ev_ci), useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(time == 48) |>
  pull(Cc)
css_closed <- r0 / paper_cl(81)
stopifnot(abs(css_typ / css_closed - 1) < 0.01)

ci48 <- sim_dev |>
  filter(treatment == "16 g/day continuous infusion", time == 48) |>
  mutate(css_cf = r0 / cl)
# Every subject: concentration at 48 h within 5% of its own R0 / CL. The bound
# covers subjects with slow distribution (small kpc) still approaching
# steady state.
stopifnot(quantile(abs(ci48$Cc / ci48$css_cf - 1), 0.9) < 0.05)

tibble(
  Quantity = c("Typical Css, closed form (mg/L)", "Typical Css, model at 48 h (mg/L)", "Cohort median Css at 48 h (mg/L)"),
  Value = c(css_closed, css_typ, median(ci48$Cc))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "16 g/day continuous infusion, typical patient at 81 mL/min and 69 kg.")
```

# PKNCA

Felton 2014 reports no non-compartmental results, so the PKNCA summary below is
a characterisation of the packaged model for each intermittent regimen of the
estimation data set rather than a comparison. The single dose uses the full
48 h; the multiple-dose regimens use the last simulated dosing interval.

```{r pknca}
# Subjects with very fast elimination reach concentrations at the level of the
# ODE solver tolerance late in the 48 h window, which can come back as tiny
# negative values; they are set to zero before NCA.
conc_dev <- sim_dev |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), treatment != "16 g/day continuous infusion") |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_dev <- ev_dev |>
  filter(evid == 1L, treatment != "16 g/day continuous infusion") |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals <- tribble(
  ~treatment, ~start, ~end, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life, ~cmin,
  "2 g over 30 min, single dose", 0, 48, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE,
  "4 g over 30 min q6h", 42, 48, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,
  "3 g over 4 h q8h", 40, 48, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_dev, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_dev, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = as.data.frame(intervals)
))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cmin")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

# Robust centre check on the single dose: the median AUC0-inf must sit near
# the cohort's median Dose / CL (CL is linear, so AUC0-inf = Dose / CL exactly
# per subject).
cl_sd <- sim_dev |>
  filter(treatment == "2 g over 30 min, single dose") |>
  distinct(id, cl)
auc_sd <- nca_tab$aucinf.obs[nca_tab$treatment == "2 g over 30 min, single dose"]
stopifnot(abs(auc_sd / median(2000 / cl_sd$cl) - 1) < 0.05)

nca_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Regimen = treatment, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUCtau (mg*h/L)" = auclast, "AUC0-inf (mg*h/L)" = aucinf.obs,
    "t1/2 (h)" = half.life, "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters per regimen (200 virtual patients each).")
```

# Figures not replicated

Figs. 3 to 6 of Felton 2014 show Bayesian forecasts made by the BestDose
software for the 8 validation patients, each from that patient's posterior over
the NPAG support points. The support points (the Pmetrics density file) and
the validation patients' individual covariates and dosing records are not
published, so those individual forecasts and the dose recommendations of
Table 4 cannot be reproduced from a parametric model.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Only the final model is packaged.** Table 2 lists four structural models,
  but parameter estimates are published only for the linear model with
  covariates (Table 3), the model the authors used in the dosing software.
* **Mean column as typical values.** Table 3 gives the mean, median and SD of
  each NPAG marginal without saying which describes a typical patient. The
  means reproduce the Fig. 4 first-dose observations of the validation cohort
  within 2-fold from 2 h on, whereas the medians fall more than 3-fold short,
  so the means were used (section "Mean or median as the typical value").
* **Log-normal IIV from the marginal SDs.** NPAG estimates a discrete joint
  density. Each marginal is approximated by a log-normal centred on the
  reported mean with `omega^2 = log(1 + (SD/mean)^2)`. The joint shape,
  including any multimodality and any correlation between parameters, is not
  reported and is not represented; the etas are independent. For `kcp` and
  `kpc` the marginals are strongly skewed (mean several times the median), so
  the log-normal is a coarse approximation.
* **Each intercept and slope carries its own eta.** In a nonparametric fit
  every one of the six parameters is a subject-level random quantity, so the
  creatinine-clearance slope and the weight slope have their own IIV, as in
  the Table 3 SDs.
* **Creatinine clearance in mL/min.** The Fig. 2 legend gives `Cls` "in liters
  per hour" without a covariate unit. Table 1 reports Cockcroft-Gault
  creatinine clearance in mL/min, and only that reading gives a plausible
  typical clearance (13.3 L/h at the cohort mean) and concentrations in line
  with Fig. 4; reading it in L/h would leave 6-h concentrations near 50 mg/L
  against observations of 2-15 mg/L. Rate constants are taken as 1/h, the
  time unit of the data.
* **Residual error.** The assay error polynomial `SD = 1.04 + 0.14 x C` was set
  by the authors before fitting and is encoded with `combined1()`, the
  linear sum that Pmetrics uses. Pmetrics also multiplied the variance by a
  fitted scalar gamma whose value is not reported; the encoded error
  corresponds to gamma = 1 and is likely an underestimate.
* **Validation covariates.** The Roberts validation patients' individual
  creatinine clearance and weight are not published, so the virtual validation
  cohort was drawn from the Table 1 summary (mean, median and range), and the
  Fig. 4 observations were digitised by eye from the published raster.
* **Literature check.** No erratum or correction for Felton 2014 was found in
  Europe PMC (checked November 2026), and the article has no supplementary
  material.
